title: Load snapshot index and investigation canvas for performance anomalies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a durable snapshot index and an 'investigation canvas' UI that lets SREs and performance engineers quickly compare benchmark runs, surface regressions (tokens/sec, p95 latency), and guide an anomaly investigation workflow. Current problem: benchmark artifacts are scattered across blob stores with inconsistent metadata, making pairwise comparisons slow and blocking fast rollbacks during incidents. This ticket implements a compact snapshot index, deterministic diff keys, a comparison payload format, and a front-end canvas for evidence-driven investigation.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot index stores metadata for every benchmark run (model, revision, sequence_profile, batch_config, hw_type, run_timestamp) and is queryable by time range and tag
Comparison payload includes aggregated metrics (tokens_sec, p95, p50, p99, tokens_cost, batch_size) and raw sample traces for failing shards
UI canvas supports side-by-side run comparison, heatmap of token throughput over time, p95 distribution overlay, and a compact regression score (0-100)
Automated diff runner flags regression candidates and posts findings to the perf-alerts Slack channel with reproducible run links
Benchmarks can be replayed from the comparison canvas with the same env/config and produce a reuseable run_id for triage
Documentation (Confluence) and runbook for the investigation canvas is written and linked from the UI
tasks: Design compact snapshot index schema and retention policy (S3 prefix layout + small Parquet metadata)
Implement server-side indexer that annotates uploads with deterministic diff_keys
Add regression scoring library (tokens/sec drop %, p95 delta normalized by historical noise)
Create REST endpoints for query, compare, and replay orchestration
Prototype React canvas: timeline, overlay charts, raw trace drilldowns, and action buttons (replay, open PR, assign)
Wire alerting: perf-regression rule -> Slack + issue template
Add telemetry: clicks, reproduce success rate, and time-to-resolution metrics
notes: We should aim for a snapshot index entry size < 2KB to keep listing/querying cheap
Consider using a bloom filter for quick existence checks across large run sets
Historical noise baseline must be computed per model+sequence_profile to avoid false positives
Replay orchestration should reuse existing load-test k8s job templates from ENG-45812
Canvas design needs to favor evidence first: show p95 and tokens/sec deltas alongside sample traces before raw logs
